verses.english: Linked Discourses 7.11
2. Lay Followers
With Bhāradvāja the Farmer
So I have heard.

verses.pali: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā magadhesu viharati dakkhiṇāgirismiṁ ekanāḷāyaṁ brāhmaṇagāme.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Magadhans in the Southern Hills near the brahmin village of Ekanāḷa.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena kasibhāradvājassa brāhmaṇassa pañcamattāni naṅgalasatāni payuttāni honti vappakāle.
verses.english: Now at that time the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Farmer had harnessed around five hundred plows, it being the season for sowing.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena kasibhāradvājassa brāhmaṇassa kammanto tenupasaṅkami.
verses.english: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to where Bhāradvāja the Farmer was working.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena kasibhāradvājassa brāhmaṇassa parivesanā vattati.
verses.english: Now at that time Bhāradvāja the Farmer was distributing food.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā yena parivesanā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
verses.english: Then the Buddha went to where the distribution was taking place and stood to one side.

verses.pali: Addasā kho kasibhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ piṇḍāya ṭhitaṁ.
verses.english: Bhāradvāja the Farmer saw him standing for alms
and said to him,

verses.pali: “ahaṁ kho, samaṇa, kasāmi ca vapāmi ca, kasitvā ca vapitvā ca bhuñjāmi.
verses.english: “I plough and sow, ascetic, and then I eat.

verses.pali: Tvampi, samaṇa, kasassu ca vapassu ca, kasitvā ca vapitvā ca bhuñjassū”ti.
verses.english: You too should plough and sow, then you may eat.”

verses.pali: “Ahampi kho, brāhmaṇa, kasāmi ca vapāmi ca, kasitvā ca vapitvā ca bhuñjāmī”ti.
verses.english: “I too plough and sow, brahmin, and then I eat.”

verses.pali: “Na kho mayaṁ passāma bhoto gotamassa yugaṁ vā naṅgalaṁ vā phālaṁ vā pācanaṁ vā balībadde vā, atha ca pana bhavaṁ gotamo evamāha:
verses.english: “I don’t see the worthy Gotama with a yoke or plow or plowshare or goad or oxen, yet he says:

verses.pali: ‘ahampi kho, brāhmaṇa, kasāmi ca vapāmi ca, kasitvā ca vapitvā ca bhuñjāmī’”ti.
verses.english: ‘I too plough and sow, brahmin, and then I eat.’”

verses.pali: Atha kho kasibhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
verses.english: Then Bhāradvāja the Farmer addressed the Buddha in verse:
“You claim to be a farmer,
but I don’t see you farming.
Tell me how you’re a farmer when asked:
how am I to recognize your farming?”
“Faith is my seed, fervor my rain,
and wisdom is my yoke and plough.
Conscience is my draft-pole, mind my strap,
mindfulness my plowshare and goad.
Guarded in body and speech,
I restrict my intake of food.
I use truth as my scythe,
and gentleness is my release.
Energy is my harnessed beast,
transporting me to sanctuary from the yoke.
It goes without turning back
to where there is no sorrow.
That’s how to do the farming
that has freedom from death as its fruit.
When you finish this farming
you’re released from all suffering.”
“May the worthy Gotama eat!
The worthy one is a farmer.

verses.pali: Yañhi bhavaṁ gotamo amatapphalampi kasiṁ kasatī”ti.
verses.english: For the worthy Gotama does the farming that has freedom from death as its fruit.”
“Food enchanted by a verse isn’t fit for me to eat.
That’s not the principle of those who see, brahmin.
The Buddhas cast aside things enchanted with verses.
Since there is such a principle, brahmin, <j>that’s how they live.
Serve with other food and drink
the consummate one, the great seer,
with defilements ended and remorse stilled.
For he is the field for the seeker of merit.”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, kasibhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When he had spoken, the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Farmer said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama …
From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
